preamble: No regular historical or allophonic change of the voiceless uvular stop /q/ to the plain alveolar stop [t] has been found. The only case on file is an error pattern in child speech: in Ibbi Yemeni Arabic acquisition data, /q/ is fronted to the emphatic (pharyngealized) alveolar [tˤ], not to plain [t]. Child substitutions are developmental errors rather than sound changes of a speech community, and the outcome sound differs, so this cell is effectively unattested.

examples.note: Developmental fronting reported for children aged 1;9 to 3;6; the outcome is emphatic [tˤ] rather than plain [t]. Example carried over from the earlier entry; the paper is paywalled and the form was not re-checked.

sources: Alfaifi, A., & Qasem, F. (2024). Phonological substitution patterns in Yemeni Ibbi Arabic child speech: a markedness and natural phonology perspective. Cogent Arts & Humanities 11(1). https://doi.org/10.1080/23311983.2024.2360795
